n: Elder and Vulnerable Customer Financial Abuse
ds: Older or vulnerable people are exploited by relatives, carers, scammers or persons holding power of attorney. Warning signs include sudden changes in banking behaviour and the presence of third parties directing transactions.

src.t: FinCEN, Advisory on Elder Financial Exploitation (2022)
UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (specify year, e.g. 2025)
FCA, Guidance for firms on the fair treatment of vulnerable customers (FG21/1, 2021)

cn.rt: Third parties, carers or attorneys directing withdrawals, term deposit breaks and borrowing; branch and phone staff are key detection points.

rat: Third-party directed withdrawals and transfers; branch intervention.

ind.cx: Victim-side: unusual cash or transfers inconsistent with usual pattern.
ind.ds: Transactions or withdrawals are uncharacteristic of, or inconsistent with, the customer's known profile, income or expected activity.

ind.n: Third party accompanies and directs the customer
ind.cx: Another person speaks for the customer or dictates instructions.
ind.ds: Another person speaks for, accompanies or dictates instructions to the customer, who may appear fearful, scripted or unable to explain the activity.
ind.cn: Customer accompanied, directed or coached by a third party

ind.n: New joint account holder or power of attorney added
ind.cx: Access given to a new person shortly before unusual activity.
ind.ds: Access given to a new person shortly before unusual activity.

ind.n: Confusion or fear about own finances
ind.cx: Customer appears unsure of balances, recent transactions or reason for payments.
ind.ds: Customer appears unsure of balances, recent transactions or reason for payments.

ind.n: Sudden new spending on unrelated person
ind.cx: Frequent payments or purchases benefiting a carer or acquaintance.
ind.ds: Frequent payments or purchases benefiting a carer or acquaintance.

ind.n: Frequent ATM use by carer or unusual card use
ind.cx: Cards used where customer is unlikely to be present.
ind.ds: Cards used where customer is unlikely to be present.

ind.cx: Victim-side: repeated scam payments or telephone contacts.
ind.ds: repeated scam payments or telephone contacts.

ind.n: Changes to statements delivery, address or contact
ind.cx: Mail redirected to a third party.
ind.ds: Email, phone, address or statement delivery details are changed, especially shortly before unusual activity or redirecting mail to a third party.
ind.cn: Recent change of contact or delivery details

ind.n: Property or investment sold under pressure
ind.cx: Large assets liquidated with hurried instructions.
ind.ds: Large assets liquidated with hurried instructions.

ctl.ds: Analyses typing, navigation, remote-access tooling, call-in-progress signals and deviation from baseline to spot coached, scripted or hijacked sessions. It detects coercion and takeover.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.

Allows customers to nominate a trusted contact and applies tailored handling and permitted escalation when vulnerability is flagged. It adds a safeguard for customers more exposed to manipulation or coercion.
Verifies instructions, detail changes and unusual requests by contacting the customer on a channel held on file, never one supplied in the request. It defeats impersonation and account takeover.

ctl.n: Account detail change monitoring and cool-down
ctl.ds: Contact, device or payee changes trigger notification to the prior channel and restrict risky actions for a short period, with alerts on clusters of changes. It disrupts takeover.

Reviews and updates customer information on a risk-based cycle and when triggers occur, such as ownership change, key attribute change, adverse information or out-of-profile activity. Fresh data keeps risk ratings and expected-activity baselines current.

Provides targeted messaging that helps customers recognise scam scripts and mule recruitment, verify requests independently and use trusted routes for giving or paying. It reduces victimisation and unwitting participation.
Tracks cases, outcomes, losses and false positives, routes concerns across fraud, sanctions and anti-corruption teams and feeds outcomes into tuning and appetite. It supports consistent handling.

ctl.n: Cooling-off and delayed release for new payees
ctl.ds: Holds or delays the first large payment to a new payee or to changed details so the customer or institution can verify before funds leave. It buys time to detect coercion or fraud.

ctl.n: Dynamic payment friction and scam warnings
ctl.ds: Risk-scored payments trigger a purpose question and a tailored scam warning, or a call-back, before release to the customer. It gives the customer a chance to reconsider and interrupts payments made under deception.
